terms: ## Conversational Texture The user reviewed the option comparison, explicitly picked B-incremental for its zero-under-review-risk property, and directed development through the full Lattice flow. A standing directive applies: no Chinese in any documents or code, including any emitted strings (everything English-only). The REVIEW->TEST gate and binding semantics must not change -- this story only enriches the reviewer's input.

## Key Insights Reviewer verdicts already record the headHash they were bound to (core/review-run.ts captureReviewRunSnapshot). git already exposes per-file blob hashes, and changedFilesBetween / a plain git diff between two commits is available (core/evidence-freshness.ts). So 'what changed since reviewer X last passed' is computable from existing data with no new persistence. The skip/carry-forward variant (B-skip) was rejected: an LLM reviewer's true dependency set is not statically provable, so skipping a reviewer can never reach hard-zero under-review risk. B-incremental never skips, so the gate stays identical and under-review is impossible by construction.

## Solution Tradeoffs B-incremental (chosen): every reviewer still runs every round and still produces a fresh verdict (gate unchanged), but is fed only the diff since its last pass plus its prior verdict, so each re-run is cheaper. Pros: zero added under-review risk, small additive surface, no gate/binding change. Cons: still spawns every reviewer each round (saving is per-reviewer work, not fewer reviewers). Rejected alternative B-skip: carry forward unaffected reviewers -- larger saving but irreducible under-review risk. Rejected alternative: do nothing and rely on the existing converge-fixes-into-few-commits discipline plus the B-cfdd advisory -- zero cost but leaves each re-run doing redundant full analysis.

## Trigger Event On 2026-06-16, while driving B-cfdd (the soft convergence-stall advisory) the team confirmed the re-review cost mechanism: each finding-fix commit changes the source tree, stales every reviewer's binding (one global materialHash in core/evidence-freshness.ts), and forces a fresh round where every active reviewer re-analyzes the whole diff from scratch. The user evaluated three ways to cut that cost and chose B-incremental specifically because it carries ZERO added under-review risk.

Add a smoke (packages/main/src/tasks style): (a) a reviewer with a prior pass gets the since-last-pass diff; (b) a first-time reviewer gets the full diff; (c) ASSERT the REVIEW->TEST gate still requires every active reviewer to have a fresh current-round verdict -- the helper changes nothing about binding/staleness/skip (drive or stub the gate path to show an absent current-round verdict still blocks). Wire the smoke into the validate/test chain. Update CLAUDE.md REVIEW section to document the incremental-context helper and the unchanged-gate invariant.

Each REVIEW re-review round re-runs every active reviewer, and each reviewer re-analyzes the entire git diff main...HEAD from scratch even though only a small part changed since it last passed. This makes re-review rounds expensive. Scope (the B-incremental variant, deliberately chosen over the skip/carry-forward variant to keep ZERO under-review risk): add a read-only helper that, for a given (storyId, reviewer role), returns that reviewer's most recent prior verdict plus the incremental diff since the headHash that verdict was bound to (falling back to the full diff main...HEAD when the reviewer has no prior pass). Surface a hint in the round>=2 story_advance REVIEW output telling each reviewer to pull its incremental context and re-confirm only what changed since it last looked. CRITICAL INVARIANT: no reviewer is ever skipped and the REVIEW->TEST gate is UNCHANGED -- every active reviewer still produces a fresh current-round verdict whose binding is validated exactly as today. This change only makes each reviewer's WORK cheaper (smaller, targeted input), never reduces the set of reviewers, so it cannot cause under-review. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: skipping or carrying-forward any reviewer (the rejected B-skip variant); any change to the gate / binding / materialHash / staleness logic; changing what each reviewer reviews; the convergence-stall advisory (B-cfdd, already done). All artifacts and any emitted strings are English-only.
Expose it (lattice review_incremental_context) and hint it in the round>=2 REVIEW-entry output

For a given (storyId, reviewer role), resolve that reviewer's most recent prior review-run/verdict and the headHash it was bound to (core/review-run.ts records headHash; review-passes.json / findings.json hold the verdict). Compute the incremental diff between that headHash and current HEAD (reuse the git-diff approach from core/evidence-freshness.ts changedFilesBetween / done-effects diff helpers). If the reviewer has no prior pass (first time), fall back to the full diff main...HEAD. Pure/read-only: no writes, no gate side effects.
Make REVIEW re-review rounds cheaper via per-reviewer incremental context (zero skip, gate unchanged)
Read-only incremental-context helper: prior verdict + diff since the reviewer's last-pass headHash
Tests + docs; assert the REVIEW->TEST gate semantics are unchanged (no skip, fresh verdict still required)

Wire the helper as a read-only CLI command lattice review_incremental_context --storyId --role=<reviewer> (English-only output). In handlers/transition-effects.ts, when entering REVIEW for round >= 2, append a hint line telling reviewers to run that command first and re-confirm only what changed since their last pass. Keep the hint advisory; it must not change the transition result. Do NOT touch the gate / binding / canPassReview.
entries.reason: Superseded: INIT review (INIT-001) revealed the REVIEW->TEST gate is more lenient than this story assumed (Round 1 requires all opt-in reviewers + quorum; Round 2+ requires only >=1 valid current-round receipt). Recreating with the corrected merged option-2 scope: incremental-context helper PLUS round-2+ informed targeted re-review guidance, gate unchanged.
